summary: Audit-trail artifact in code-research.md §4 meets test/audit-quality bar for the docs-actualization feature. Coverage: §4 term set (SHA3, SHA-3, sha3, mcp-server-rs, pre-V1, Pre-V1, HashEmbedder, Python backend, mcp-server.py) is a strict superset of the user-spec term set (user-spec line 22, 77, 163; tech-spec line 136) and matches Task 2 step-1 grep verbatim. Per-hit table (§4.3): all 6 pre-flight hits (DRAG_ANALYSIS:37; WEB_RESEARCH:45/64/132; CONCURRENT_WRITERS:157/217) carry file/line/original/replacement/verdict columns with concrete before/after content (no placeholders) — original quotes are exact line text and replacements specify either deletion semantics or token substitutions with rationale. Audit-trail completeness: 3 newly-discovered hits in recovered/competitive-landscape/README.md (lines 8/9/10) are recorded in §4.2 with classification 'keep' and explicit rationale (upstream narrative about the validation work), then deferred to a Task 4 owner-driven README rewrite — proper escalation. Cross-check against current core/+mcp/ is documented (zero hits; sha384 deep-hash false positive disambiguated). Verifiability: §4.2 includes the exact grep command and §3 the restoration command; future agent can reproduce — I re-ran the documented grep and got identical output (6 in-content + 3 README hits). Closing paragraph at line 91 asserts run date 2026-04-27 and result counts. Acceptance criteria: grep -c 'replace-token' = 8 (>=6), grep -c 'Sanity-grep run completed' = 1 — both pass. Term-set extension policy from user-spec R2 is honored (term set extensible; explicit conclusion 'term set unchanged from pre-flight' at line 72).

findings.issue: DRAG_ANALYSIS:37 'Replacement' column describes the action narratively ('delete the entire line ...') rather than showing literal after-text (which is the empty/elided form). All other 5 rows show post-replacement substring quotation, making this row mildly inconsistent for an automated diff against the audit trail during Wave 3 promotion (Task 4).
findings.suggestion: Optional: append the literal post-state — e.g., 'After: <line removed>' or show the surrounding lines that remain — so a future agent can pattern-match audit-trail entries to actual file diffs uniformly. Non-blocking; the verdict 'replace-token (delete-line variant)' and the rationale are sufficient for human review.

findings.issue: Cross-check section at line 72 states 'zero hits for SHA3|sha3|HashEmbedder|mcp-server-rs|Pre-V1|pre-V1|Python backend|mcp-server.py' — this enumerates 8 of the 9 terms from the term set; 'SHA-3' (with hyphen) is implicitly covered but not explicitly listed in the cross-check enumeration. Minor consistency gap in the audit-trail wording.
findings.suggestion: Optional: add 'SHA-3' to the cross-check enumeration for parity with §4 term set, or note 'all 9 terms' instead of enumerating. Non-blocking; the actual grep regex covers SHA-3 correctly via 'SHA3' pattern overlap is not present, but in practice 'SHA-3' is rare and the documented pre-flight inventory shows zero SHA-3 hyphenated occurrences.

findings.issue: Closing paragraph reports '6 in-content hits across 3 files (plus 3 narrative mentions in recovered/competitive-landscape/README.md classified keep)'. Task-2 closing-paragraph template said 'Total <N> hits across <M> files'. Keeping the in-content / narrative split is clearer, but a strict template-matcher could mis-parse total counts. Numerically correct (9 raw / 6 in-content / 3 narrative).
findings.suggestion: Optional: add an explicit total line, e.g. 'Total 9 raw hits (6 in-content for replace-token; 3 narrative kept).' Non-blocking — the existing wording is unambiguous on careful reading and the numbers are reproducible from the documented grep.
